games.title: Aeon of Strife
games.note: A fan-made StarCraft map: each player controls one powerful hero while computer troops push down lanes. Its creator is disputed.

games.title: Defense of the Ancients
games.note: A Warcraft III map begun by Eul and grown by Guinsoo and then IceFrog into DotA Allstars, the template for MOBAs.

games.title: Dota 2
games.note: Valve hired DotA's anonymous lead designer IceFrog in 2009 to make it.

games.title: Smite
games.note: A third-person MOBA in which you play gods from world mythologies.

games.title: Heroes of the Storm
games.note: Blizzard's MOBA, with shared team levels, several maps and heroes from Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo and Overwatch.

games.title: Honor of Kings
games.note: Tencent's phone MOBA, one of the most played games in China; its international version was called Arena of Valor.

games.title: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang
games.note: Hugely popular in Southeast Asia, especially Indonesia and the Philippines.

games.title: Pokémon Unite
games.dev: TiMi Studio Group / The Pokémon Company
games.note: The first Pokémon MOBA: teams score points by dunking energy into goals instead of destroying towers.

games.title: Dota Auto Chess
games.note: A fan-made Dota 2 custom game that drew over eight million players within months and started the auto-battler genre.

games.title: Dota Underlords
games.note: Valve's own auto-battler with Dota heroes; early access from June 2019.

games.title: Hearthstone Battlegrounds
games.note: An eight-player auto-battler mode inside Hearthstone, using its minions and heroes.

games.title: Mahjong
games.note: A tile-matching game that took shape in China in the 19th century; its exact origin is debated.

games.title: Rampart
games.note: Repair castle walls with Tetris-like pieces, place cannons, then fire on attacking ships, in timed phases.

games.title: Desktop Tower Defense
games.note: A Flash game in which your towers form the maze the enemies must walk; it won an Independent Games Festival award.

games.title: Bloons Tower Defense
games.note: Dart-throwing monkeys pop waves of balloons; a spin-off of Ninja Kiwi's Flash game Bloons.

games.title: Plants vs. Zombies
games.note: George Fan's lawn-defense game; Laura Shigihara wrote the music, including the credits song 'Zombies on Your Lawn'.

games.title: Insaniquarium
games.note: George Fan's aquarium game, where you feed fish, collect coins and fight off alien invaders; PopCap published it.

games.title: Magic: The Gathering
games.dev: Richard Garfield / Wizards of the Coast
games.note: Richard Garfield's collectible card game, the first of its kind.

games.title: Tapper
games.note: A bartender slides drinks down four bars to customers who keep coming.

games.title: Kingdom Rush
games.note: Made in Montevideo, Uruguay; it began as a Flash game and sold over seventeen million copies on phones.

games.title: Dungeon Defenders
games.note: Co-op tower defense played as third-person heroes who level up and collect loot.

games.title: Orcs Must Die!
games.note: Made by former Age of Empires developers: a war mage fills fortress corridors with traps and slices orcs himself.

games.title: Sanctum
games.note: Coffee Stain's breakthrough from Skövde, Sweden: build tower mazes, then fight beside them in first person.

links.took: StarCraft's units, engine and the map editor with scripted triggers that shipped with it.
links.added: Each player controls a single hero against waves of computer-controlled units.
links.extra: A custom map made with StarCraft's own tools.

links.took: One hero per player, lanes of computer troops and bases to destroy.
links.added: Heroes that level up, items, and Night Elf 'Ancient' buildings as the bases to defend.

src.t: Game Developer, Postmortem: Defense of the Ancients

links.extra: Eul remade Aeon of Strife in Warcraft III's engine.

links.took: Warcraft III's hero units, creeps, engine and World Editor.
links.added: A five-against-five map of three lanes where the whole match revolves around heroes.
links.extra: Built as a custom map for Warcraft III and its Frozen Throne expansion.

links.took: One player-controlled commander at the center of a two-sided battle.
links.added: Hero levels, items and three lanes of computer-controlled troops.
links.extra: Genre histories cite Herzog Zwei as a forerunner of the MOBA; no DotA developer has said so.

links.took: The DotA formula and one of its key designers, Steve Feak (Guinsoo).
links.added: A standalone free-to-play game with matchmaking, a growing roster and a friendlier learning curve.
links.extra: Wikipedia says League was initially designed by Steve Feak, one of DotA Allstars' creators.

links.took: DotA Allstars' heroes, items, map and look.
links.added: A standalone game with better servers, statistics and reconnecting.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls it heavily inspired by DotA Allstars.

links.took: DotA's heroes, map and rules, and its lead designer IceFrog.
links.added: Valve's Source engine, matchmaking, spectating and a cosmetics economy.
links.extra: Valve hired IceFrog in 2009.

links.took: The lane-pushing hero battle format that DotA popularized.
links.added: A third-person camera, aimed abilities and gods from world mythologies.

links.took: The five-against-five hero battle format DotA popularized.
links.added: Shared team experience, no item shop and many maps with their own objectives.
links.extra: Blizzard settled a 2012 dispute with Valve over the DOTA name before renaming its project.

links.took: StarCraft II's engine; the game began as a Blizzard-made custom map for it.
links.added: A standalone hero brawler using characters from all of Blizzard's games.

links.took: The free-to-play MOBA that League made into one of the world's biggest games.
links.added: Matches cut to around fifteen minutes and controls built for phones.
links.extra: Tencent owns Riot Games and also published Honor of Kings.

links.took: League's five-against-five lane battles, adapted for phones.
links.added: Short matches, simple touch controls and a huge following in Southeast Asia.
links.extra: Riot Games sued developer Moonton in 2017, alleging it copied League of Legends; Moonton disputed the claim.

links.took: TiMi Studio Group's experience making a hit phone MOBA.
links.added: Pokémon that evolve during a match and goals you score in instead of towers.
links.extra: Same developer.

links.took: Dota 2's engine, custom game tools and heroes.
links.added: Eight players draft heroes from a shared pool and place them on a chessboard to fight automatically.
links.extra: Built as a Dota 2 custom game.

links.took: Drawing from a shared pool and combining matching pieces into stronger sets.
links.added: Matching three copies of a hero upgrades it, and the sets fight on a board.

src.t: Wikipedia: Auto battler (cites 'How mahjong inspired this popular PC game')

links.took: The whole auto-battler loop: shop, bench, board placement, class synergies and gold interest.
links.added: League of Legends champions, a shared item carousel and a polished standalone client.

src.t: Riot Games, via PC Gamer, June 2019

links.extra: Auto Chess came out in January 2019; Riot announced TFT in June, saying Auto Chess inspired it.

links.took: The auto-battler format of drafting Dota heroes onto a board.
links.added: A standalone release for computers and phones with cross-play.
links.extra: Valve and Drodo each made their own standalone versions in 2019.

links.took: Dota 2's heroes and world.
links.added: Turned them into pieces in an auto-battler with City Crawl progression.
links.extra: Same studio, Valve.

links.took: Eight-player auto-battler rounds of buying units and watching them fight.
links.added: Hearthstone's minions and heroes, each hero with its own power.
links.extra: Auto Chess launched in January 2019; Blizzard added Battlegrounds that November as its own take on the genre.

links.took: Hearthstone's minions, heroes, art and client.
links.added: An eight-player auto-battler mode instead of one-on-one card duels.

links.took: Placing defenses to stop waves of attackers, the core Rampart established.
links.added: Towers that also form the maze the enemies must walk through.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Rampart is generally considered to have established the prototypical tower defense.

links.took: Tower defense, which Warcraft III's custom maps made hugely popular.
links.added: A free browser game anyone could play in minutes.

links.took: Tower defense, which Warcraft III's custom maps made hugely popular.
links.added: Monkeys, balloons that split into smaller balloons and a fixed winding track, free in a browser.

links.took: Monkey towers popping waves of balloons.
links.added: 3D graphics, hero units and three upgrade paths for every tower.

links.took: Browser tower defense, popularized by Desktop Tower Defense.
links.added: Fantasy towers you upgrade along branches, heroes and barracks soldiers who block paths.

links.took: George Fan imagined a more defense-oriented version of his own aquarium game.
links.added: Plants that defend lawn lanes against a comic zombie invasion.
links.extra: Same designer.

links.took: Tower defense, after George Fan played Warcraft III tower defense mods.
links.added: Five lanes, sunlight as currency and an approachable game for non-gamers.

links.took: Card-game ideas, including choosing a hand of seed packets before each level.
links.added: Plant 'cards' with cooldowns and sun costs, played in real time.
links.extra: Fan played Magic with composer Laura Shigihara.

links.took: Juggling several lanes at once as threats move along them.
links.added: A lawn of five or six lanes filled with plants instead of beer mugs.

links.took: Mixing tower defense with a hero you control directly.
links.added: A first-person shooter view: you build a maze of towers, then fight inside it.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Sanctum popularized the shooter hybrid pioneered by earlier games such as Dungeon Defenders.

links.took: Action tower defense with a playable hero, which Dungeon Defenders popularized.
links.added: Traps instead of towers, and a cocky war mage who fights in third person.

links.took: Coffee Stain's first-person building on an alien planet.
links.added: A factory and conveyor-belt game in an open world instead of tower defense.
links.extra: Same studio.
